en: 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith and Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to us, both from 'Abd as-Samad—and the wording is that of 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd as-Samad: my father narrated to us, from my grandfather, from al-Husayn ibn Dhakwan: Ibn Buraydah narrated to us: 'Amir ibn Sharahil ash-Sha'bi, of the Sha'b branch of Hamdan, narrated to me that he asked Fatimah bint Qays, sister of ad-Dahhak ibn Qays, and she was among the early emigrant women: He said: 'Narrate to me a hadith that you heard directly from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), attributing it to no one else besides him.' She said: 'If you wish, I shall certainly do so.' He said to her: 'Yes indeed, narrate to me.' She said: 'I married Ibn al-Mughirah, and he was among the best of the youth of Quraysh at that time, but he was struck down in the first jihad with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When I became a widow, 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf, along with a group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), proposed to me. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) proposed to me on behalf of his freed slave, Usamah ibn Zayd. And it had been narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever loves me, let him love Usamah." So when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) spoke to me, I said: "My affair is in your hand, so marry me to whomsoever you wish." He said: "Move to Umm Sharik." And Umm Sharik was a wealthy woman from the Ansar who spent greatly in the cause of Allah, at whose house guests would stay. So I said: "I will do so." But he said: "Do not do that, for Umm Sharik is a woman who has many guests, and I dislike that your head covering should fall off or the garment should uncover your shins so that people might see some of you that you dislike. Rather, move to your cousin 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, Ibn Umm Maktum"—and he was a man from Banu Fihr, the Fihr of Quraysh, and he was from the same sub-clan that she belonged to—'so I moved to him. When my waiting period was completed, I heard the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) announcing: "The prayer is in congregation!" So I went out to the mosque and prayed with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I was in the row of women that directly followed the backs of the men. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concluded his prayer, he sat upon the pulpit smiling and said: "Let every person remain in his place of prayer." Then he said: "Do you know why I gathered you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "By Allah, I did not gather you out of desire nor out of fear, but I gathered you because Tamim ad-Dari was a Christian man who came, pledged allegiance, and embraced Islam, and he narrated to me a narration that agreed with what I had been narrating to you about the False Messiah. He narrated to me that he sailed in a sea vessel with 30 men from Lakhm and Judham, and the waves tossed them about for a month at sea. Then they anchored by an island in the sea just at sunset. They sat in the small rowboats of the ship and entered the island, where they were met by a beast that was hairy and coarse-haired, such that they could not tell its front from its back because of the abundance of its hair. They said: 'Woe to you! What are you?' It said: 'I am al-Jassasah.' They said: 'And what is al-Jassasah?' It said: 'O people, go to this man in the monastery, for he is longing to hear your news.' He said: When it named a man for us, we became terrified of it lest it be a female devil. He said: So we set off quickly until we entered the monastery, and behold, inside it was the largest human being we had ever seen in physical build, and the most severely shackled, with his hands bound together to his neck, and between his knees to his ankles in iron. We said: 'Woe to you! What are you?' He said: 'You have been able to discover my news, so tell me who you are.' They said: 'We are people from the Arabs. We boarded a sea ship and encountered the sea when it was stormy, so the waves tossed us about for a month, then we anchored by this island of yours. We sat in its small rowboats and entered the island, where we were met by a beast that was hairy and coarse-haired, such that one could not tell its front from its back because of the abundance of its hair. So we said: "Woe to you! What are you?" and it said: "I am al-Jassasah." We said: "And what is al-Jassasah?" It said: "Proceed to this man in the monastery, for he is longing to hear your news." So we came to you quickly, terrified of it, not feeling safe that it might be a female devil.' He said: 'Tell me about the date-palms of Baysan.' We said: 'About which aspect of them are you asking?' He said: 'I ask you about its date-palms: do they bear fruit?' We said to him: 'Yes.' He said: 'Beware, soon they will not bear fruit.' He said: 'Tell me about the Lake of Tiberias.' We said: 'About which aspect of it are you asking?' He said: 'Is there water in it?' They said: 'It has abundant water.' He said: 'Beware, soon its water will disappear.' He said: 'Tell me about the spring of Zughar.' They said: 'About which aspect of it are you asking?' He said: 'Is there water in the spring, and do its inhabitants irrigate with the water of the spring?' We said to him: 'Yes, it has abundant water, and its inhabitants irrigate from its water.' He said: 'Tell me about the Prophet of the unlettered: what has he done?' They said: 'He has departed from Mecca and settled in Yathrib.' He said: 'Did the Arabs fight him?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'How did he deal with them?' So we informed him that he had prevailed over those of the Arabs near him, and they obeyed him. He said to them: 'Has that really happened?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Beware, indeed it is better for them to obey him. And I am going to inform you about myself: I am the Messiah, and soon I will be permitted to emerge. So I will emerge and travel through the earth, leaving no town without entering it within 40 nights, except Mecca and Taybah; both of them are forbidden to me. Whenever I intend to enter either one of them, an angel meets me with an unsheathed sword in his hand, barring me from it. And indeed, at every mountain pass of it there are angels guarding it.' She said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, striking the pulpit with his staff: 'This is Taybah, this is Taybah, this is Taybah'—meaning Medina—'Behold, did I not use to narrate that to you?' The people said: 'Yes.' 'For indeed, the narration of Tamim pleased me, as it agreed with what I used to narrate to you about him, and about Medina and Mecca. Behold, is he not in the Syrian Sea or the Yemeni Sea? No, rather from the direction of the East is he, from the direction of the East is he, from the direction of the East is he!' and he pointed with his hand toward the East. She said: 'I preserved this from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'
